results.reasoning: A first look (unprefixed evidence in the same folder) failed this rule: a person's signed pass from before the design request read human: stale, but its per-role acceptance stayed signed, so after an agent re-judge the rule read verified and nobody was asked. lib/status.js now applies the same design floor to the acceptance entry, and this second look re-drove the whole rule through the CLI on throwaway projects with their own WALKDOWN_HOME (person pat, two rules on receipt, one on cart). The request was filed with threads new --reason request and accepted two ways, by pat's walkdown (finishWalkdown) and by threads set --status verified as pat. Every step held: an open request staled nothing; after acceptance the agent verdicts and pat's pre-request verdicts on both receipt rules read stale with designAccepted, in the human cell and in acceptance; cart and checks were untouched; after an agent re-judge the rule read pending and NEEDS A HUMAN asked pat to walk it again; fresh passes after acceptance passed; pat's verdicts given while the request was open stood, including the walk that accepted the design and approvals over three walks; a legacy verified request with no verified_at and no verifier reply staled nothing. Edges weighed and reported, not filed: the per-rule view labels a design-staled signature as signed an older wording (about 50%), and acceptDesigns counts a pre-request signature toward the set (about 60%). Below 10%: an agent verdict in the same second as the acceptance reads current. No server or port was used.
